provenance: DERIVED -- empirically observed from applied design files, not read from an authored brand guide. Confidence is lower than the other 4 case studies' synthesis.json files, which cite an actual written brand document. Treat as a starting hypothesis for a real brand guide, not a substitute for one.

colors.name: Gold / khaki accent
colors.value: approx. #A18C45 - #A79F57 (varies slightly by piece/print vs. digital rendering)
colors.usage_notes: The one color that recurs across every piece sampled except the Advancement and Service social graphics: dominant in Billboard, Magazine Ad, and Recruitment Cards, and present as a secondary tone in the Leadership social graphic (#A38F61, #CDC0B1). Reads as the primary brand accent -- plausible real-world fit for a military/veterans brand (bronze medal / brass insignia association).
source_files: Design Deliverables/Media Kit/Social Media Graphics/Ready To Use JPEGs/VFW_Leadership__1.jpg

colors.name: Near-black overlay/background
colors.usage_notes: Appears as the top dominant color in every single sample (PDF and JPEG alike). This is very likely a dark photo-overlay/vignette treatment applied consistently across all deliverables, not a flat 'brand color' per se -- but the consistency itself is a real, derivable style rule (see imagery_style below).

colors.name: Advancement pillar accent (red)
colors.usage_notes: Only sampled in the single Advancement social graphic -- may be a pillar-specific accent (VFW's Media Kit Guide defines three pillars: Leadership, Service, Advancement) rather than a universal brand color. Unconfirmed with only one sample; would need to check VFW_Advancement__2-5.jpg to see if it's consistent across the pillar.
source_files: Design Deliverables/Media Kit/Social Media Graphics/Ready To Use JPEGs/VFW_Advancement__1.jpg

colors.name: Service pillar accent (blue)
colors.usage_notes: Only sampled in the single Service social graphic -- same caveat as the Advancement accent: plausibly a per-pillar accent color, unconfirmed beyond one sample.

typography.usage_notes: Embedded in the Magazine Ad PDF. Paired with Roboto/Roboto Condensed in the same piece -- likely serif for a pull-quote or headline treatment against sans-serif for body/labels.
Embedded in the Magazine Ad PDF alongside PT Serif.

Embedded in both the Magazine Ad and the Recruitment Cards PDFs -- the only typeface confirmed in more than one deliverable, making it the strongest candidate for 'the' brand typeface if only one had to be named.

imagery_style.description: Every sampled piece (billboard, magazine ad, and all three pillar social graphics) shows a strong dark overlay/vignette over photography as the single most dominant color in a histogram sample -- consistent enough across unrelated formats (print billboard vs. social JPEG) that it reads as a deliberate, repeated treatment rather than coincidence.

other_notes.description: Both Illustrator preflight reports (Billboard, Magazine Ad) specify CMYK color mode with the 'U.S. Web Coated (SWOP) v2' color profile -- standard commercial print spec. No spot colors were declared in either report (empty 'Spot Color Objects' section), meaning color is managed via CMYK process, not brand-locked Pantone spot colors.

Billboard and both T-shirt PDFs returned zero embedded font objects via pdffonts -- their text was converted to vector outline paths before export (consistent with the sibling '-paths.ai' file that exists for Billboard). This means typography for those specific pieces can't be confirmed from the PDF alone; the Magazine Ad and Recruitment Cards fonts above are the only directly-confirmed typefaces.
